prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposed policies (non-ideological)

Economy and jobs
- Invest in renewable energy, home insulation and green infrastructure; target 90% renewable electricity by 2030 and net zero by 2045.
- Industrial strategy focused on future skills, AI, bioscience and clean tech; restore stability via independent fiscal oversight.
- Support SMEs: abolish business rates and replace with a Commercial Landowner Levy; expand British Business Bank; tackle late payments; develop local banking.
- Skills: replace apprenticeship levy with a flexible skills levy; Lifelong Skills Grants (£5,000 per adult); boost apprenticeships and National Colleges.
- Employment rights: create a “dependent contractor” status; 20% higher minimum wage for zero-hours at normal demand; right to request fixed hours; reform Statutory Sick Pay; establish a Worker Protection Enforcement Authority.
- Tax measures: reverse previous bank tax cuts; stronger windfall tax on oil and gas; raise Digital Services Tax to 6%; fairer capital gains; 4% tax on FTSE-100 share buybacks; future priority to raise the personal allowance when affordable.

Health and social care
- Right to see a GP within seven days (24 hours if urgent); recruit 8,000 GPs; expand pharmacy roles and a universal 24/7 booking system.
- Restore access to NHS dentistry for urgent care; preventive measures for child oral health.
- Mental health: walk-in hubs for young people everywhere; regular mental health check-ups at key life stages; a qualified mental health professional in every school.
- Cancer: 100% start treatment within 62 days from urgent referral; more radiotherapy machines; more cancer nurses.
- Invest in public health, digital interoperability, diagnostics and hospital estates; improve ambulance response; Patients’ Charter.
- Drug policy: health-led approach, expand treatment; legal, regulated cannabis market for adults.
- Social care: introduce free personal care; workforce plan, a Royal College of Care Workers and a carers’ minimum wage (+£2/hour); paid carers’ leave and regular respite; sustainable funding settlement; independent living focus.

Education and families
- Increase per-pupil funding above inflation; rebuild unsafe estates; tutoring guarantee for disadvantaged pupils.
- Early years: more free hours for disadvantaged children; triple Early Years Pupil Premium; restore maintenance grants; Lifelong Skills Grants for adults.
- Teacher recruitment/retention strategy; curriculum and Ofsted reform; stronger SEND funding and a national body.
- Families: extend free school meals to all children in poverty; overhaul parental leave—double statutory maternity/shared pay to £350, add a paid month for partners at 90% pay; make parental leave/pay day‑one rights including for the self‑employed.

Environment, food and farming
- End sewage discharges via tougher regulator, penalties and a sewage tax; real-time water data; social water tariff.
- “Double nature” by 2050; 60 million trees/year; Clean Air Act with an Air Quality Agency; 30% of land and sea protected by 2030; deposit return scheme; phase out non‑recyclable single-use plastics.
- Food strategy to improve security, affordability and nutrition; accelerate and properly fund Environmental Land Management; protect standards in trade; veterinary and plant health agreements with Europe; strengthen the Groceries Code Adjudicator; research fund including alternative proteins; comprehensive Animal Welfare Bill.

Housing, communities and transport
- Build 380,000 homes/year (150,000 social); new garden cities; reform land compensation; abolish leasehold and cap ground rents; ban no‑fault evictions; default three‑year tenancies; national landlord register; end rough sleeping; remove dangerous cladding at no cost to leaseholders.
- Empower councils on second homes/short lets; multi‑year local funding; nationwide gigabit broadband.
- Transport: nationwide EV charging rollout, plug‑in grant, 2030 zero‑emission sales requirement; freeze rail fares; rail electrification, Northern Powerhouse Rail; bus franchising and £2 fare cap while reviewed; active travel expansion; shift more freight to rail; reform aviation taxes and curb short domestic flights where rail is viable.

Rights, democracy, crime and immigration
- Human Rights Act upheld; Digital Bill of Rights; ban conversion practices; bolster services for survivors of violence; flexible working as a right; disability inclusion and UNCRPD in law; assisted dying free vote.
- Political reform: proportional representation (STV), votes at 16, cap donations, statutory Ministerial Code, Lords reform, citizens’ assemblies, stronger transparency.
- Policing and justice: community policing; guarantee police attendance for burglaries; Online Crime Agency; court backlog reduction; rehabilitation focus; stronger modern slavery protections; improved cooperation with European agencies.
- Immigration and asylum: end hostile policies; scrap Rwanda plan; three‑month service standard; right to work after three months; expand safe and legal routes; flexible, sector‑informed work visas; fair family visa rules; Windrush redress; limit detention; enhance Youth Mobility.

Defence and international
- Increase defence spending towards 2.5% of GDP; reverse Army cuts; maintain nuclear deterrent; stronger procurement and parliamentary oversight; tighter arms export controls.
- Rebuild European ties via phased roadmap (including veterinary agreements and mutual recognition), long‑term aim of Single Market membership; support Ukraine including using seized Russian assets; restore aid to 0.7% with poverty focus; fund BBC World Service; support two‑state solution and immediate bilateral ceasefire in Israel‑Gaza; targeted human‑rights sanctions.
